answer: Sharing a box makes cheap keys look abundant. Require every address to finish a private inference job before the same cutoff. A verification kernel builds that job from the epoch seed and the key, so a sibling's output fails the check. Size the work so one accelerator completes only one job in time — a design assumption, not a benchmark. If that costs about $0.80 of GPU time, 200 clones spend about $160 each cycle and need 200 cards running together. One card is a tight canyon; a second voyage does not finish before cutoff.
